results.message: Is the two-recension theory of De Unitate right?

voice_event.speaker: lpc
voice_event.text: We do not know. Chapters 4-5 of De Unitate survive in two versions. One, the 'Primacy Text', reads more favourably toward Roman primacy. The other does not. The claim that the Primacy Text is a later hand's work, and not Cyprian's own, is held among us as Contested. That means we have weighed it and found it unresolved. We do not know which version Cyprian wrote first, or whether he wrote both. Nothing in our own account here rests on that question being closed. What we do hold is this: the episcopate is one office, and each bishop holds his part for the whole. Cyprian argued that from what the Lord said to Peter. It is an argument from scripture, not a traced succession. Whether the Primacy Text is his or not, that conviction is.

citations.sentence: Chapters 4-5 of De Unitate survive in two versions.

sources.label: De Unitate 4-5 survives in a single authorial text, and the version of chapters 4-5 commonly called the 'Primacy Text' -- reading more favourably toward Roman primacy than the alternative recension -- is a later interpolation into Cyprian's own original wording, not evidence of anything Cyprian himself wrote or revised.

sources.citation: Cyprian of Carthage, On the Unity of the Church (De Unitate), Ante-Nicene Fathers, vol. V

names.name: Thascius Caecilius Cyprianus, bishop of Carthage (248/249-258)

figures_used.bridge_line: Our bishop, chosen while still new to the faith, over his own reluctance. During a plague he taught us to love even our enemies. He was put to death under Valerian.

dates.display: a trained rhetorician who turned from a public career to Christian life, converted c. 246; ordained and elected bishop of Carthage between roughly July 248 and April 249 by the acclamation of the Carthaginian people, over the recorded opposition of five presbyters, while still newly baptised, as his deacon Pontius tells it; banished to Curubis under the Valerianic persecution; executed under the emperor Valerian in 258
